query_text: Under the modeled gas-injection conditions, what maximum pore pressure can fault F2 in the Asmari reservoir sustain, and how do the three fault-stability formulations characterize it?
expected_answer: The study estimates a maximum pore pressure of 55–57 MPa for F2. The 3-D Mohr-diagram, slip-tendency and modified-slip-tendency approaches identify F2 as the most stable of the studied faults. This is a conditional model estimate, with pre-existing faults treated as cohesionless, not an operational safety guarantee. In order to reach stress criticality we have to assume zero cohesion, as illustrated in one of the key wells (well 6) or increase the pore pressure significantly.
